page: Microsoft Azure F2amds_v7 is an x86_64 virtual machine belonging to the Famdsv7 server family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 2 dedicated physical cores and 2 vCPUs powered by an AMD EPYC 9V45 processor operating at a clock speed of 4.5 GHz. The hardware configuration includes 16.0 GB of system memory, yielding an 8.0 GB per core ratio, which classifies this instance as memory-intensive. Local storage is provided via a 236 GB disk, and the instance is capable of utilizing Premium Storage. No GPUs are included in this configuration, and it comes with zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark data reveals strong single-core performance, with stress-ng single-core CPU performance, Geekbench single-core score, and single-threaded gzip compression all placing in the top 10% tier. However, multi-core and multi-threaded scaling show limitations due to the 2-core hardware boundary. Multi-core stress-ng CPU performance, Geekbench multi-core score, and Passmark CPU scores fall into the average category. Multi-threaded bzip3 decompression and software compilation with Clang are positioned in the bottom 25% tier. Memory bandwidth tests show average performance, with read-only small block cached bandwidth at 420.17 GB/sec and large block uncached write bandwidth at 30.22 GB/sec.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the F2amds_v7 offers high single-thread compute capabilities and a dense memory-to-core ratio, making it suitable for memory-bound workloads that do not require massive parallelization. Tradeoffs include poor performance in medium-sized LLM inference tasks, where prompt processing for a 7B model falls into the bottom 10% tier, and weak static web serving throughput. This server is suited for database operations, text processing, and lightweight single-threaded applications, but is less optimal for parallelized compilation, ray tracing, or large-scale LLM deployment.
